summary: When fighting suddenly escalated around Taiz, in southwestern Yemen two months ago, midwife Anisa Fadhl had no time to pack a bag before she fled, leaving behind her home and her clinic. Both were later looted and destroyed.

summary: Years of insecurity, violence perpetrated by murderous armed gangs and economic instability, combined with displacement, poor agricultural performance and climate shocks, have left millions of Haitians struggling to meet their food needs.

summary: The 21m tree is Oslo’s annual thank you for Britain’s support during World War Two.

title: Bridgetown AI summit to tackle safety as risks outpace capacity to respond
summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres is heading to Barbados to co-host a special summit on artificial intelligence (AI) safety on Monday, aimed at closing the gap between accelerating risks and many countries’ capacity to deal with the pace of development.

title: ‘You will not be alone’: General Assembly President tells Rohingya refugees after genocide ruling
summary: A day after the UN’s highest court found that Myanmar had committed genocide against the Rohingya, the President of the General Assembly visited the refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, urging the world to turn the landmark judgement into action.

title: West Bank: Record settler attacks mar olive harvest as UN urges Israel to protect farmers
summary: Israeli settlers have carried out more than 400 attacks causing casualties or property damage during this year’s olive harvest in the occupied West Bank – more than in any previous season, UN agencies and humanitarian NGOs said on Friday.

title: WFP plans to assist 91 million in 2027 as hunger crisis deepens
summary: The World Food Programme (WFP) will require $12.1 billion to assist 91 million people next year but warned that millions more will go hungry as funding shortfalls continue and another global food crisis looms.

title: COP31: Countries demand stronger climate deal amid deadlock in Antalya
summary: A group of countries from Europe, Africa, Latin America and the Pacific has challenged the proposed COP31 agreement, demanding explicit action on fossil fuels and stronger climate finance. With the summit due to close on Friday, tensions are rising as activists warn the talks are headed for failure, and negotiators search for a deal that nearly 200 governments can accept.

title: Afghanistan restrictions prevent pregnant women from seeking medical help
summary: Aid and development agencies in Afghanistan warned on Friday of an escalating “assault” on the rights and freedoms of women and girls that is preventing growing numbers from accessing vital medical care.

title: Battle to control GPS and radio signals raises civilian safety concerns
summary: From aid convoys in conflict zones to passenger jets and cargo ships far out at sea, safe journeys depend on GPS, satellite navigation and old-fashioned radio transmissions. But these signals are increasingly being blocked or faked – and civilians are paying the price.

title: ‘Losing the battle’: AI hands predators new ways to target children
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is handing predators and criminal groups new ways to groom, extort and exploit children, while efforts to protect them are failing to keep pace, senior UN officials warned on Thursday.

title: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
summary: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.

title: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
summary: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.

title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
summary: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

title: COP31: The push to protect warming oceans reaches the negotiating table
summary: From identifying marine life with a cup of seawater to drawing on Indigenous knowledge to prevent wildfires, scientists and communities showcased both cutting-edge and time-tested ways to protect nature at COP31 on Tuesday. Yet turning innovation into action remains a challenge, with funding gaps persisting and ministers struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance as negotiations enter their final days.

title: Haiti: ‘Atrocious abuses’ continue as UN warns anti-gang operations must priortise civilian protection
summary: The UN human rights office, OHCHR has urged greater protection for civilians in Haiti amid ongoing “atrocious abuses” committed by gangs and intensified security operations.

title: Winter rains deepen Gaza crisis amid restricted access and aid cuts
summary: Gaza is facing a deepening shelter, sanitation and food security crisis as winter rains flood makeshift shelters, destroy scarce food supplies and leave displaced families struggling to stay warm and fed.

title: Lebanon leading the way in mental health support
summary: Mental health support must be a core part of the humanitarian response, said the UN Deputy Secretary-General during a visit to Lebanon over the weekend, where efforts to address the psychological toll of years of conflict and instability offer valuable lessons for other crisis-affected countries.

title: Syria: Progress ‘real’ but fragile, as remnants of war wreck young lives
summary: Syria is showing “undeniable signs of progress” nearly two years after the fall of the Assad regime, but explosive ordnance, the approaching winter and severe funding shortfalls threaten those fragile gains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Monday.

title: COP31 enters decisive week as climate talks face political test and AI initiatives gather pace
summary: New international initiatives on artificial intelligence and green industrialization showcased technology’s growing role in climate action, even as negotiators remained deadlocked on finance, fossil fuels and adaptation ahead of the final stretch of the UN talks.
